Every contiguous sideLength-by-sideLength square contains exactly one cell from each row-and-column residue pair, so selecting at most `maxOnes` residue classes yields a feasible periodic matrix. For residue r, the arithmetic formula counts exactly r, r + sideLength, and subsequent coordinates within the relevant dimension; multiplying row and column counts gives that class's complete contribution, including partial boundary tiles. Selecting the `maxOnes` greatest independent contributions therefore realizes the global optimum.

A literal binary-matrix oracle enumerated every matrix and checked every contiguous constrained square for all 48 legal parameter combinations with width and height through three. A separate oracle scanned every full-matrix coordinate into residue frequencies without using the protected arithmetic formula. Both agreed with protected and immutable native sources on all ten authored cases, all three benchmark outputs, 13,026 legal combinations with width and height through twelve, and 10,000 deterministic random inputs generated with seed 1183.

Random validation included 711 zero-allowance inputs, 697 full-residue allowances, 863 unit side lengths, 7,837 partial-width tiles, 7,794 partial-height tiles, 9,903 rectangles, 97 squares, 107 maximum widths, 106 maximum heights, and 831 cases whose side length equaled the smaller dimension.
